title: [ROCm][MI350P] Muse Spark MonoKernel decode assumes 256 co-resident CTAs (MI355X); refused on 128-CU MI350P
scope:
### Summary

The Muse Spark AMD MonoKernel specialized-decode path added in #62766 is hard-wired to MI355X's **256** compute units. On an MI350P (`gfx950`, **128** CUs, 16 shader engines) the runner refuses the model outright, and the path cannot run even though the part is the same ISA (`gfx950`).

This issue scopes what it would take to support MI350P. No GPU workload was run; the analysis is from the source and from `rocminfo` device properties.

### Root cause

The decode kernels use a persistent, fully co-resident cooperative grid: **one CTA per CU, every CTA resident**, with CTAs spin-waiting on each other's mailbox hand-offs. A spin-wait on a non-resident CTA can never make progress, so the grid width must equal the resident-CTA capacity of the GPU.

`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/specialized_decode/mono/spec.py` (and `mono/common/plan.py`):

```python
# One CTA per CU of an MI355X, all of them co-resident -- a spin wait on another
# CTA can only make progress if that CTA is running, so the runner refuses a GPU
# with another CU count -- and THREADS threads each.
BLOCKS = 256
```

The runner gate in `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py` (`platform_reasons`):

```python
cus = current_platform.num_compute_units(...)   # multi_processor_count
if cus < BLOCKS:
    # every CTA of a launch must be resident: a partitioned GPU deadlocks
    return [f"{cus} CUs (the kernels need {BLOCKS} resident CTAs, one a CU)"]
```

On MI350P `num_compute_units()` returns 128, so `128 < 256` fires and the path is refused with `"128 CUs (the kernels need 256 resident CTAs, one a CU)"`. The `on_gfx950()` arch gate passes (MI350P *is* `gfx950`); only the CU-count gate fails.

### Why this is not a one-line constant change

The per-CU resource budget is identical between the two parts (same `gfx950` CU: 160 KiB LDS, 256 VGPR, 2-wave occupancy), so each CTA's budget is unchanged — but you cannot pack 2 CTAs per CU (each CTA already consumes a whole CU's LDS and a 2-wave VGPR occupancy). So `BLOCKS` genuinely has to drop to 128 on MI350P; keeping 256 is physically impossible to co-reside.

Dropping `BLOCKS` to 128 breaks the static task-to-CTA placement, which is derived from `BLOCKS = 256` throughout `spec.py`. Structural invariants that fail at `BLOCKS = 128`:

- `O_TASKS == 2 * BLOCKS` — 512 o_proj tasks over 128 CTAs is 4 per CTA, not 2.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Share one RoPE cache across Muse Spark NVIDIA layers
scope:
_Requested by **Simon**_



## Overview

The NVIDIA Muse Spark model builds a private fp32 RoPE table in each of its 46 RoPE attention layers. The tables are identical and cost 11.5 GiB per GPU. This PR shares one table, as #62757 did for the ROCm path.

Fixes #65205

## Claims

- Model loading drops from 81.0 to 69.75 GiB per GPU on 8x B200, TP8, `Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`.
- The KV cache grows from 9,248,688 to 10,589,618 tokens (+14.5 %).
- Output does not change: greedy output is bit-identical, and GSM8K-100 is 96/100 on stock and 95/100 with this PR, which is within run-to-run noise.

## Validation

New unit test `tests/models/test_muse_spark_nvidia_shared_rope.py`, CPU only, with the heavy submodules stubbed. It mirrors `test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py` from #62757.

- Two target layers must hold the same fp32 `RotaryEmbedding`.
- It uses its own empty `_ROPE_DICT`, so the CPU tables it builds do not leak into later GPU tests (the failure #65138 and #65140 fixed for the ROCm twin).

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest -v tests/models/test_muse_spark_nvidia_shared_rope.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py \
  tests/models/test_muse_spark_logits_local.py
```

On this branch: 16 passed. Without the model change, the new test fails (two different objects). The test is added to the "Basic Models (Other)" step next to its ROCm twin.

End to end on 8x B200, TP8, `unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`, default `max_model_len` (1,048,576), with prefix caching. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-76c6f3f2a95f6049657db1e513133b824a5c8175` (digest `sha256:7a933b7c…`), the newest nightly; no nightly at this base exists yet. `nvidia/model.py` is byte-identical on 76c6f3f2a and this PR's base, so the PR arm loaded this branch's `nvidia/model.py` on that image. Each arm ran on a fresh server start, and each start logged the sha256 of the file that was loaded.

| Check | Stock | This PR |

| Model loading per GPU | 81.0 GiB | 69.75 GiB |
| Available KV cache memory, TP0 | 90.01 GiB | 101.26 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 9,248,688 tokens | 10,589,618 tokens (+14.5 %) |
| Greedy, 8 prompts × 256 tokens, one at a time | reference | 8/8 bit-identical |
| GSM8K-100, temperature 0, 32 concurrent | 96/100 | 95/100 |

title: [AMD][MI35X] Add Muse Spark Open vLLM monokernel AgentX config / [AMD][MI35X] 新增 Muse Spark Open vLLM monokernel AgentX 配置
scope:
## Summary

vLLM now ships a FlyDSL decode monokernel for Muse Spark Open on MI355X (vllm-project/vllm#63440, merged 2026-11-02). InferenceX has no vLLM point for this model on MI355X, so its AgentX curve only shows SGLang. This PR adds one: TP8 with expert parallel, `--monokernel`, the seven-token DSpark draft, at the same concurrencies as the SGLang TP8/EP8 arm (1, 4, 8, 13).

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-40941f2c4ba96fba0a7e282a5355e89cd74d9ac5`, digest-pinned. It is the newest nightly (2026-11-03) and is 96 commits past the #63440 merge.
- Server flags and environment follow the command validated in #63440: `ROCM_AITER_FA`, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC`, `AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16`, `max-num-seqs 16`, 1M context, prefix caching.
- New provisional golden curve `musespark_dspark.yaml`: the sweep's connector needs a curve for `musespark` + `dspark` and none exists. It carries DFlash2's K=7 value (4.05) and is labeled provisional, as `glm5.3_mtp.yaml` is. It must be replaced with a SPEED-Bench measurement on `Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark`.

## Risks and open items

- The golden AL (4.05) is not measured with DSpark. Real acceptance with `--monokernel` is reported as 4.25-4.42 against 4.69 for the stock path in #63440 (the kernels keep MoE activations in bf16), so throughput points assume a better acceptance than evals will see.
- The SGLang TP4/EP4 DRAM-offload arm (c10-c40) is not mirrored. The monokernel needs TP8 and no KV offloading, and there is no validated vLLM offload recipe for this model yet.
- Steps of more than 16 requests (rows above 128) and prefill-carrying steps run the stock path.
- The sweep starts only once a maintainer applies a primary sweep label.

Not an InferenceX run. Same server flags on 8x MI355X from the #63440 head (not this image), synthetic acceptance 4.05, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`, c1: interactivity p50 485.6 / p90 452.0 (ITL p50 2.06 ms, p90 2.21 ms). #63440 reports GSM8K 0.9689-0.9757 at c1-c8.

</details>

title: perf(amd): pack speculative verify rows in gfx950 mha decode
scope:
## Summary

- Before: speculative verify launched one gfx950 MHA decode work-group per query token, so an 8-token verify block streamed every KV page 8 times. The sliding-window split merge also read partials with volatile loads, which bypass the caches.
- Now a request's queries of one KV head form max_seqlen_q x group-size rows, and a work-group takes up to 64 of them (one 16-row MFMA tile per wave), so its waves share every K and V page.
  - Each row masks its own causal end and window start; split counts follow requests, not query tokens.
  - The launcher rejects q rows that are not a multiple of max_seqlen_q, which the per-request grid would leave unwritten.
  - Sliding windows of at most 16 pages use one-wave 16-row blocks with at least two pages per split; longer windows keep their tiles and splits.
  - The sliding merge loads partials normally; the split's acq_rel counter increment already orders them.
- Numerics: plain decode is bitwise unchanged on 106 of 120 shapes; the rest change split count or group size with reference error unchanged or within 4.9e-4.
- Applies to gfx950 MHA decode with max_seqlen_q > 1 (verify), plain decode under short sliding windows, and multi-split sliding decode.
- Measured effect, microseconds per layer, graph replay:
  - Muse Spark TP8 8-token verify (MI355X): bs16 8k full 74.2 → 20.2, sliding 56.7 → 17.0; bs4 50k full 110.0 → 30.5. Sliding decode (window 2047) bs1 50k 24.3 → 20.3 cold, from the cached-load merge.
  - Beam TP8 16-token verify, window 512 (MI355X): 14-71% faster at 4+ requests, slower at 1-2 (8.3 and 9.8 → 10.4 and 10.6). GPT-OSS TP4 verify 25-38% faster; GPT-OSS sliding plain decode 23-55% faster (MI350X).
  - Muse Spark TP8 and EP1 with DFLASH, 8x MI355X, 8k input: TPOT C1 1.274 → 1.251 ms, C16 6.91 → 5.97 ms.

## Test Plan

- Rebased onto main and re-run on 8x MI355X at the top of the gfx950 attention stack: gfx950 MHA kernel suites (decode, decode spec, FP8, extend, prefill) 345 passed, batch-shape recompile suite 21 passed, runtime MHA warmup, decode-schedule and query-dtype tests 11 passed. The split into this stack was checked on CPU (compile, `pre-commit run --all-files`).
- New decode tests cover 2-16 query positions, padding rows, two row blocks per KV head, head dim 128, sinks, short and long windows (including mid-page starts), graph replay of refreshed lengths, and one compile per request b

title: fix(amd): keep gfx950 mha prefill/extend correct and compiled at startup
scope:
## Summary

- Causal prefill with more requests than one round of work-groups holds (512 / query heads): empty slots of the last round read `cu_seqlens` past the batch and wrote stray rows into the output, or faulted. Slots past the batch are now inactive.
- Prefill compile keys held the request count, max_seqlen_q and token strides, so fresh prompts recompiled the causal and sliding kernels on the forward thread (3.4-3.7 s each). The request count is now a runtime argument, and the launcher makes Q, K and V contiguous (copying only a packed-QKV view of V).
- Extend kernels never ran at startup (the warmup prefill has no cached prefix) and specialized on num_seqs, so each variant compiled while serving (0.6 s on every rank). `warmup_gluon_mha_extend_gfx950` now compiles every tile, depth, grid and split class, and the MHA backend's `kernel_warmup` runs its cached-prefix extend on the warmup prefill's rows.
- Numerics unchanged for every batch the old code handled correctly.
- Applies to gfx950 MHA prefill and extend; the warmup extend runs on every platform whose MHA plan reports postwrite.
- Measured effect: no compiles while serving Muse Spark TP8 with DFLASH, at no kernel cost on MI355X (prefill within 1.2%, extend within 0.6%).

## Test Plan

- Rebased onto main `c242ed0ce` and re-run on 8x MI355X at the top of the gfx950 attention stack: gfx950 MHA kernel suites (decode, decode spec, FP8, extend, prefill) 345 passed, batch-shape recompile suite 21 passed, runtime MHA warmup, decode-schedule and query-dtype tests 11 passed; at this PR's tip the runtime warmup test passes (2 passed). The split was checked on CPU (compile, `pre-commit run --all-files`).
- A 40-request prefill with poisoned trailing `cu_seqlens` fails on the old code; prefill and extend sweeps over batch shapes compile nothing after one warm launch (old code: 5 and 7-10 binaries); a CPU test checks the warmup extend runs once with the layer's window.
